ci integration

Exit codes

Every DevOpsGen command exits with a stable, documented status code so shells, scripts and CI jobs can branch deterministically — no output parsing required.

CodeClassificationMeaningTypical example
0successEverything requested completed; dry-run plans that resolved cleanly also end here.init created 5 files; --dry-run --force plan is green.
1general errorUnexpected failure — I/O errors, template issues, or a run that failed mid-write and rolled back.Disk full while writing deployment.yaml.
2invalid inputConfiguration failed validation before anything was planned or written.--image BANGKAH/my-app; port -1; Ingress without host.
3conflictTarget files already exist and would be overwritten; nothing was written. Retried with --force.Second init without --force.
4validation failedGenerated documents exist but do not pass static lint rules.Unpinned workflow action in ci.yaml.
5detectionStack detection was ambiguous or found nothing at all.Empty directory without go.mod / package.json.

In practice

shell script branching
devopsgen init --stack go --registry ghcr --image you/myapp --port 8080
case $? in
  0) echo "ready" ;;
  3) devopsgen init --force --stack go --registry ghcr --image you/myapp --port 8080 ;;
  2) echo "fix your flags" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "see devopsgen validate output" >&2 ;;
esac
Codes are part of DevOpsGen's compatibility promise: bumping a major version may add new codes, but existing ones keep their meaning.
